t: Apply Operations to Make All Array Elements Equal to Zero — Window Greedy
o: Each operation subtracts 1 from a contiguous window of exactly length k; we ask whether some multiset of operations zeroes the array. Greedy insight: process left to right; the leftmost nonzero element nums[i] must be reduced by exactly nums[i] - (decrements already covering it) operations, and every one of those operations must start at index i (any window starting earlier would have been forced earlier; starting later wouldn't cover i). So that many windows [i, i+k-1] are mandatory — possible only if nums[i] is divisible by k and i + k <= n. Track how many active decrements cover each position with a difference array. Example [2,2,3,1,1,0], k=3 succeeds as shown; [1,3,1,1], k=2 fails since 1 is not divisible by 2.
k: The leftmost uncovered deficit forces windows starting exactly at that index.
Each position's residual must be nonnegative and divisible by k, and the window must fit inside the array.
A difference array tracks how many ongoing k-windows still cover the current index.

a.i: Sweep left to right carrying 'cur' = total decrements currently applied at this index (windows started within the last k indices). The residual r = nums[i] - cur must be zeroed by new windows starting at i; require r >= 0, r % k == 0, and i + k <= n. Schedule r windows by adding r to cur and scheduling its removal at i + k via a difference array.
s: Initialize diff array of size n+1 and cur = 0.
At index i: cur -= diff[i]; r = nums[i] - cur.
If r < 0, r % k != 0, or i + k > n (when r > 0), return false.
Otherwise cur += r and diff[i + k] += r; return true after the scan.
a.t: O(n) — one pass, constant work per index.

w: There is essentially one idea here; the difference array is the clean implementation (a deque of expiring amounts works identically). Key correctness point: forcing windows to start at the leftmost deficit never hurts, since any valid solution's windows covering that index can be shifted left without harming earlier (already-zero) positions. Watch overflow in C++/Java (use long long / long) since values reach 1e6 and n reaches 1e5. Edge cases: k = n (whole-array windows only), all zeros (true), last k-1 elements must be exactly covered by earlier windows. Follow-up: minimize the number of operations instead of feasibility (answer = sum of residuals / k with the same greedy).
